subject: Pilot playbook and pricing collar — usage definitions & true-up cadence
messages:
From: Lydia Ramos <lydia@octanehealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Whitaker <tom.whitaker@octanehealth.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Feb 2027 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Pilot scope & commercial guardrails for evaluation

Hi Karthik —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We put together a short MAP template (attached) to capture the pilot milestones and the expected commercial guardrails. High level asks from our side:

- 30-day pilot starting after SOW execution; pilot acceptance criteria = 95% classification accuracy on our test prompts and successful integration with our patient-data pipeline (no PHI stored in Redwood).
- Clear ramp plan and capped spend for pilot (we want to avoid surprise overages while testing).
- Pricing collar or ramp corridors during the first 6 months to protect us from early volatility as we move to committed volume.
- True-up cadence preference: quarterly (we can do monthly during pilot if you insist, but quarterly is preferable from our procurement lens).
- Price protection: we want protection across the model family we select (not just a single quantization variant) for the first 12 months after go-live.
- Need definitions: what counts as billable usage (tokens? embeddings? streamed responses?).

Can you and your CS/legal folks take a look and provide a version that aligns with Redwood economics and any constraints from your side? We also need a redline-ready MSA if we can get to mutual terms quickly.

I've attached Octane_MAP_Template_v1.pdf and a short evaluation checklist.

Thanks — look forward to syncing.

— Lydia
Lydia Ramos
Head of Product, Integrations
Octane Health
lydia@octanehealth.com
(415) 555-0198

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Lydia Ramos <lydia@octanehealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Feb 2027 12:30:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Pilot scope & commercial guardrails for evaluation

Lydia —

Appreciate the clear template. Monica (CS) and Neha (AE) are looped in — we can move quickly on this. Initial thoughts from Redwood:

1) Pilot structure & acceptance
- We can do a 30-day pilot with the acceptance criteria you outlined. During pilot we typically provide a pilot credit (we propose a $10k credit) and a soft cap to prevent unexpected spend.

2) Pricing collar / ramp corridors
- Instead of a fixed "discount collar" we propose a ramp-collar: 3-tier per-token rates tied to achieved monthly throughput bands (Pilot, Early Ramp, Committed). This preserves predictability for both sides while giving Octane visibility into unit economics as volume increases.

3) True-up cadence
- Operationally we prefer a monthly true-up during pilot so we can reconcile usage quickly and surface issues. After the customer signs a committed annual contract we can move to quarterly true-ups if that helps procurement.

4) Price protection scope
- We are open to providing price protection across the chosen model family for 12 months, but we need to limit protection to the model family as defined in the MSA (e.g., "Llama-3-family" or "Open-XX-family") and to the selected precision modes that materially affect cost (extending across every future quantization could make sustained price guarantees unworkable). We can document permitted substitutions and fallback models.

5) Billable usage definitions
- Billable units for the proposed pilot: input tokens + output tokens for text generation; embeddings billed per vector (per call); reranking billed per candidate scored. We'll add concrete examples and a short FAQ to the playbook.

Next steps: we attached a draft Redwood_MAP_Playbook_v0.9.pdf that maps the milestone checklist to proposed economics and suggested legal language for the key clauses (true-up, price protection, overage handling). Can we schedule a 30–40 minute call to walk the playbook and pin down the true-up cadence and pilot cap?

Available slots tomorrow (Mon): 10:00–10:40 PT or 16:00–16:40 PT. If those don't work, propose 2 other times.

I'll ask legal to stand by for an initial redline based on the agreed commercial points.

Best,
Karthik
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com

From: Lydia Ramos <lydia@octanehealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Whitaker <tom.whitaker@octanehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 08:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Pilot scope & commercial guardrails for evaluation

Karthik —

Thanks for the fast reply and the playbook. A few quick clarifications from our end after reviewing:

- Quarterly true-up after close is acceptable, but we need quarterly true-ups during pilot as well (procurement wants a single cadence for the entire evaluation + ramp period). Monthly reconciliation creates too much noise for our finance team.

- Price protection: we appreciate the intent to limit to model family. To be clear, we need protection to apply across both the selected model family and the approved precision modes that we will test during the pilot (so that we don't get a surprise when we move from fp16 to an optimized int8 path). If the int8 path unlocks materially lower costs for Redwood, we can discuss sharing upside but we need a guardrail.

- Pilot cap: thank you for the $10k credit offer. We propose a hard-term cap of $15k for the pilot (Redwood absorbs anything beyond credits up to that cap) so we can test without surprises.

- Definitions: please include explicit billing examples (we'll review).

We can take the 10:00–10:40 PT slot tomorrow. I'll send a calendar invite. Attached an updated Octane_Eval_Plan.xlsx with our technical test cases.

— Lydia

Lydia / Tom —

Confirmed for 10:00 PT. Calendar invite sent. Quick note ahead of the call so we have aligned owner/action items:

Action items we will cover on the call:
- Pilot economics: agree pilot hard cap ($15k proposed by Octane) and allocation of the $10k pilot credit (applied against pilot usage; Redwood to absorb overage up to $5k).
- True-up cadence: discuss procurement preference for quarterly cadence throughout evaluation + ramp, legal to confirm billing system implications.
- Price protection and scope: legal to confirm acceptable language that protects Octane across the model family + approved precision modes for 12 months, with an explicit clause for approved substitutions and measurable notifier windows (30 days) for any model changes that could affect pricing.

Logistics & next steps post-call:
